findings.title: CloudTrail not enabled in all regions
findings.description: No multi-region trail is logging. API activity in regions you do not use goes unrecorded, which is where an attacker with stolen credentials tends to work, and there is no audit trail to investigate an incident with.
findings.remediation: Create a multi-region trail that delivers to an S3 bucket, with log file validation on, and make sure logging is started. The first copy of management events is free; you pay only for the S3 storage.

findings.title: EBS default encryption off
findings.description: EBS encryption by default is off in ap-northeast-1. Any volume or snapshot created without an explicit encryption flag stores its data in plain text, and an unencrypted snapshot can be shared with other accounts.
findings.remediation: Turn on EBS encryption by default under EC2 > Settings > Data protection and security in each region. It is free with the AWS managed key and applies to new volumes only; existing unencrypted volumes must be copied to encrypted ones.

findings.title: gp2 volume that could be gp3
findings.description: Volume vol-565cea7b0b1bf2de2 (1 GiB) is gp2. gp3 costs about 20% less per GiB and gives 3,000 IOPS at any size, where gp2 performance depends on volume size.
findings.remediation: Modify the volume and change its type to gp3. The change happens online with no downtime. For gp2 volumes larger than 1,000 GiB, set gp3 IOPS to match what gp2 provided (3 IOPS per GiB).

findings.title: Unattached EBS volume
findings.description: Volume vol-565cea7b0b1bf2de2 (1 GiB gp2) is not attached to an instance. It is billed for its full provisioned size whether or not anything uses it.
findings.remediation: Delete the volume if the data is not needed. If it might be, take a snapshot first: snapshots are stored compressed and cost much less than a provisioned volume.

findings.title: Security group open to the internet on port 22 or 3389
findings.description: Security group sg-43941006528c78d99 (default) does not expose port 22 or 3389 to the internet.
findings.remediation: Remove the 0.0.0.0/0 rule. Use Systems Manager Session Manager, which needs no inbound port at all, or restrict the rule to a known IP range or a VPN.

findings.title: GuardDuty not enabled
findings.description: GuardDuty is not enabled in ap-northeast-1. Nothing is watching CloudTrail, VPC flow and DNS logs there for signs of compromise such as crypto-mining or credentials used from an unusual place.
findings.remediation: Enable GuardDuty in every region, including unused ones, since that is where unexpected activity stands out. It has a 30-day free trial and is billed by the volume of logs analysed afterwards, so check the usage page before the trial ends.

findings.title: Root account without MFA
findings.description: The root user has MFA enabled.
findings.remediation: Sign in as the root user, open Security credentials and assign an MFA device (a passkey or hardware key is best). Then stop using root for daily work and keep it for the few tasks that require it.

findings.title: IAM user without MFA
findings.description: User example-user-1 has an MFA device.
findings.remediation: Have the user assign an MFA device under IAM > Users > Security credentials, or remove the console password if they do not need to sign in. Better still, move people to IAM Identity Center, which issues short-lived credentials.

findings.title: S3 bucket without public access block
findings.description: Bucket pillarscan-bait-fbf3f5ea does not enforce: BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets. Without these, one bad ACL or bucket policy can expose every object to the internet.
findings.remediation: Turn on all four Block Public Access settings for the bucket, or once for the whole account under S3 > Block Public Access settings for this account. Serve public content through CloudFront with origin access control instead of a public bucket.

findings.title: S3 bucket without versioning
findings.description: Bucket pillarscan-bait-fbf3f5ea has versioning off. An overwrite or delete, accidental or malicious, is then permanent.
findings.remediation: Enable versioning on buckets that hold data you cannot regenerate, and add a lifecycle rule that expires old versions so storage cost does not grow without limit.
